status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: Head coach Sean McVay said Wednesday that Adams (hamstring) returning after the Nov. 25 against the Packers "is a realistic timeline for us," Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
status.longComment: In that scenario, Adams could back in action as soon as Week 12 following the Rams' bye week. Meanwhile, Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is destined to miss multiple weeks, which, for the time being leaves Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Danielsand Xavier Smith as the healthy WRs on the team's active roster.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: Whittington (back) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.
status.longComment: This is another blow to the Rams' receiving corps, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss several weeks. Whittington would have had a chance to carve out a major role in Los Angeles' wideout room, but instead he'll be sidelined until at least Dec. 20. The Rams signed Xavier Smith off San Francisco's practice squad Tuesday to take Whittington's place on the 53-man roster and in the WR corps.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: The Rams placed Nacua (knee) on injured reserve Thursday, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
status.longComment: With this transaction officially in the books, Nacua will be required to miss at least the next four games due to the PCL and MCL sprains and turf-toe injury that he sustained near the end of this past Sunday's win at Washington. During the initial stage of Nacua's absence, the Rams will lean on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith at wide receiver until Davante Adams (hamstring) is ready to return from injured reserve.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Parkinson (ribs) was limited at Thursday's practice, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
status.longComment: While Parkinson continues to operate with a cap on his practice reps due to the rib issue that sidelined him in Week 8 against the Chargers, fellow TE Tyler Higbee showed up on Thursday's injury report as a DNP due to an illness, and reserve option Davis Allen went from limited Wednesday to no activity one day later. Friday's practice report will unveil the odds of each player to suit up Sunday at Arizona.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Allen (oblique) did not participate at practice Thursday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
status.longComment: Allen popped up on the Rams' injury report Wednesday with an oblique issue, and now his availability for Week 10 appears to be in serious jeopardy. With teammates Tyler Higbee (illness), Colby Parkinson (ribs) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) also dealing with health concerns, rookie second-rounder Max Klare currently seems to be the only Rams tight end who is a lock to suit up for Sunday's game at Arizona.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Higbee didn't practice Wednesday due to an illness, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
status.longComment: With Higbee's addition to the Rams' Week 10 injury report Thursday, the team's top three tight ends on the active roster are dealing with health concerns, as Colby Parkinson has been limited by a rib injury, while Davis Allen downgraded from limited Wednesday to no activity one day later due to an oblique issue. As a result, Friday's practice report will be telling for who among the trio may be available Sunday in Arizona.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: Rams head coach Sean McVay acknowledged Monday during his appearance on the "Coach McVay Show" that he remains optimistic Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) will return from injured reserve this season, though he was unwilling to guarantee that the tight end will be activated by the time his 21-day evaluation window closes, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports. "I'm reluctant to get too far ahead of anything, just because -- but yes, that is something we'd want to avoid if he's not prepared," McVay said, regarding the possibility of Ferguson being shut down.
status.longComment: After missing five consecutive games while recovering from an ankle sprain, Ferguson appeared poised to return from IR ahead of this past Sunday's game against the Commanders, but his activation was delayed after he pulled his hamstring while running a route during Friday's practice. McVay said after the practice that the setback would likely keep Ferguson out for "a couple more weeks." Ferguson's 21-day window will come to a close Nov. 25, so even if he doesn't resume practicing before then, he'll likely need to show the Rams that he's made at least some progress in his recovery from the hamstring injury to get activated. McVay said that he would be open to adding Ferguson back to the 53-man roster before he's ready to play, but the Rams may not be keen on essentially playing a man down for more than a game or two.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Coach Sean McVay said Monday that the Rams haven't decided whether Avila will go to injured reserve with the hamstring injury he suffered during Sunday's game at Washington, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
status.longComment: McVay said part of the decision whether to place Avila on IR will be influenced by concerns that the team could use up all of its eight injured-reserve slots for players eligible to return later in the season. Either way, for as long as Avila remains sidelined, 2024 sixth rounder Beaux Limmer projects to fill in at left guard.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Garrett (knee) practiced in a limited fashion Thursday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
status.longComment: The Rams are managing Garrett's practice reps after he returned from a seven-game absence this past Sunday at Washington, when he posted 3.0 sacks of Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will reveal if Garrett has a designation for Sunday's contest at Arizona.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: McDuffie (back) did not participate at practice Thursday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
status.longComment: McDuffie was estimated as a non-participant on the Rams' injury report Wednesday after being sidelined in Week 9 with a back injury, and his condition doesn't seem to have improved as of Thursday. Unless he's able to practice in some capacity Friday, there's a good chance he'll be out again Sunday at Arizona.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Curl (toe) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
status.longComment: It was the second consecutive DNP for Curl, who is now battling a toe injury after nearly missing the Week 9 meeting with Washington due to a foot issue. The 27-year-old might carry an injury designation heading into Week 10 against the Cardinals, but if he isn't out there, Jaylen McCollough is a candidate to replace him in the starting lineup.
